decisive_moments.reason: Pro offered a plausible conditional design—individual accountability plus interdependent group work—and directly addressed free-riding, diagnosis, access, and workload. However, it did not provide evidence that this design produces greater durability than strong individual assignments.

Con identified the central burden-of-proof problem: the argument shifted from comparative superiority to complementarity, while the added social skills were asserted to be durable without establishing retention, transfer, or comparative advantage.

Con appropriately distinguished broader outcomes from greater durability and emphasized subject-, learner-, and task-level variation. This supported the narrower conclusion that collaboration can be valuable without establishing the conjecture.

flags.quote: purposeful collaboration, integrated with individual accountability, develops a broader and more durable competence than individual grading alone
These capacities require authentic interdependence, not merely solitary practice, and transfer beyond school.
retrieval, drafting, revision, and unaided problem-solving directly test whether each learner can perform independently
